$description: Tier 1 — core (brand-agnostic) primitive tokens. PRIVATE: never reference directly in app code. Brand-IDENTITY primitives (color.primaryRamp, color.saffron, color.navy, color.yellow) live in the active brand pack (packages/tokens/brands/<id>/brand.json) so the system can be white-labelled — see brands/README.md.

green.$description: Success ramp. UNIFIED with the accent brand ramp (India Green #046A38 from the SAMAVESH logo) on 2026-08-11 — see build/brand-ramps.mjs. It was Material green #2E7D32, which sat 9 degrees and 6 L* from the logo green: two greens that close is a defect whichever token owns them. Brand-invariant (identical in Blue and Navy). Regenerate with: node build/brand-ramps.mjs then re-apply here.

red.$description: Danger ramp — full 50–900, matches SAMAVESH Figma Danger/* exactly (mode-invariant). NOTE: 700 is #b8382f (Figma) — the old code value #a11d12 was not a Figma step and is retained only as the chart.div.negStrong literal. Step 950 added 2026-08-11 for UX4G parity (11 steps); derived from this ramp’s own 500 anchor, the 50-900 steps are untouched.

amber.$description: Warning ramp — full 50–900, matches SAMAVESH Figma Warning/* exactly (mode-invariant). Step 950 added 2026-08-11 for UX4G parity (11 steps); derived from this ramp’s own 500 anchor, the 50-900 steps are untouched.

info.$description: Info hue (distinct from brand primary — Google-blue family, used in Portal DS). Step 950 added 2026-08-11 for UX4G parity (11 steps); derived from this ramp’s own 500 anchor, the 50-900 steps are untouched.

neutral.$description: Neutral grey scale — matches UX4G/SAMAVESH Figma Neutral/* variables exactly. Endpoints renumbered 2026-08-11 to match UX4G: old 1000 -> 950, old 1100 -> 1000. Pure white (0) and pure black (1000) live ONLY on the neutral ramp — they are achromatic and cannot belong to a chromatic ramp.

neutralDark.$description: NAVY BRAND neutral ramp (cooler Tailwind-family greys) — matches SAMAVESH Figma Palette/color/neutralScale/* in the Navy mode. Consumed via colorModes.navy on the neutral-derived semantic tokens. NOT a dark theme: the Navy brand renders on LIGHT surfaces, and the estate has no appearance axis at all (see apps/hub/src/app/globals.css). The key is still spelled `neutralDark` for the pre-2026-08-07 mode name; rename it with the ramp regeneration, not on its own. Endpoints renumbered 2026-08-11 to match UX4G: old 1000 -> 950, old 1100 -> 1000. Pure white (0) and pure black (1000) live ONLY on the neutral ramp — they are achromatic and cannot belong to a chromatic ramp.

space.$description: T-shirt spacing scale — matches Figma Spacing collection 1:1. Every value except 72px (8xl) is a step on the UX4G 3.0 base ramp (--ux4g-space-1…16), so this scale IS the UX4G foundation under different names; the parity layer maps the two by value. 10xl/11xl were added for UX4G padding-3xl/4xl — NEEDS FIGMA SYNC.

radius.$description: T-shirt radius scale — matches Figma Border Radius collection.

display.$description: UX4G 3.0 parity: the optical Display cut, for 36px+ headings only (--ux4g-font-family-display). Falls back to Noto Sans, so this token is safe to use before an app opts in to the extra webfont — never load it globally just to satisfy the token.
display.$value: "Noto Sans Display", "Noto Sans", ui-sans-serif, system-ui, sans-serif

mono.$description: Code, identifiers and tabular figures. IBM Plex Mono is the chosen face: open-licensed, wide weight range, unambiguous 0/O and 1/l/I, and Figma resolves it — which the previous value could not. The stack used to lead with `ui-monospace`, a CSS generic that names no font, so the Figma variable was unbindable and consequently went unused. Generic fallbacks follow for surfaces that have not loaded the webfont.
mono.$value: "IBM Plex Mono", ui-monospace, "Cascadia Code", "Source Code Pro", Menlo, monospace

size.$description: Legacy flat scale. New code should use font.role.* for the responsive role system.

role.$description: Two-surface responsive type role scale (Portal DS naming: hyphenated roles). Each size/lh/para carries mosje.type website/portal min+max bounds (min at 360px viewport, max at 1280px). The formatter emits --ds-type-ROLE-size/lh/para as clamp(min, fluid, max): Website in :root, Portal under data-surface=portal. $value is the Website desktop fallback.

tracking.$description: Letter-spacing (Portal DS naming). Website tracking is 0; Portal display tiers use negative tracking that scales with the fluid size. mosje.type website/portal min+max (px).

shadow.$description: Elevation ramp. none→xl is a 6-level superset of UX4G 3.0's 5-level l0…l4, and keeps the SAMAVESH convention of tinting toward ink (rgba(31,36,40,·)) rather than UX4G's flat black — tinted shadows read as depth instead of dirt on a light gov surface. sm/md fill the gap that previously jumped xs→lg.

motion.$description: Duration + easing primitives for transitions and animations.

border.$description: Border widths. UX4G 3.0's exact values (border-none/thin/thick/thicker/thickest), bound by name so the two cannot drift — spec §8.1 'structural' rule.

z.$description: Named stacking order. UX4G 3.0's z-index ladder verbatim — these numbers are Bootstrap's, which UX4G inherited and which third-party CSS in the estate already assumes, so diverging would put our modals under someone else's.

size.$description: One numeric size scale, VALUE-NAMED: `size/16` is 16px. Adopted from UX4G 3.0, whose 20 steps are carried at their exact rem values — the name needing no lookup is the thing worth copying, and it is what Tailwind and Spectrum do too. 22 and 44 are a SAMAVESH superset: our type scale already ships them and UX4G has no step there.

breakpoint.$description: Viewport anchors. These are not decoration: `clamp()` interpolates type between mobile and desktop, and Figma's Type modes sample the same curve at all three. The numbers were duplicated as literals in two build files until 2026-08-10 — this is now their one source.
